chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from some of his family, who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not permit Hakim ibn Hizam to engage in trade until he guaranteed for him the cancellation of the sale by the regretting buyer, the respite for the insolvent debtor, and taking the due right fully or not fully.

key_terms.إِقَالَةَ النَّادِمِ: Cancellation of sale by the regretting buyer
key_terms.حَكِيمُ بْنُ حِزَامٍ: Hakim ibn Hizam, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What are the three main conditions the Prophet Muhammad set for Hakim ibn Hizam to engage in trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s specific stipulation to Hakim ibn Hizam, emphasizing that commercial permission is contingent upon ethical conduct rather than mere legality. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Iqala* (cancellation by mutual consent) and *Inzar* (grace period for the insolvent) as core components of a just market economy, ensuring that profit does not come at the expense of social welfare.
